text:
Dylan Coghlan is back where his NHL career began. The undrafted right shot played 88 games for Vegas early on, moved through Carolina and Winnipeg, and has now dressed 17 times for the Golden Knights this season at about 14 minutes a night as a depth defenseman.

The box score is thin: two assists and no goals on 28 shots. At five on five, Vegas takes 50% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, about four points below the team without him. And the scoreboard has been very kind: Vegas has scored 8.0 more goals than its chances deserved during his shifts. That much good fortune rarely lasts.

The scouting note that matters comes from Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, over nine games last season: only 18% of his exits kept possession, so the forecheck is where to watch him. He does own a hard shot, 94.8 mph at the top (87th percentile by NHL EDGE), and he got nearly 20 minutes against Nashville on Nov. 13. On a deep blue line, the question is whether he keeps the spot.
